**Proposed mechanism:** CYP27A1 (HGNC:2410) —DISRUPTS→ bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1907265); bile acid synthesis (REACT:R-HSA-1907265) —DECREASES→ chenodeoxycholic acid (CHEBI:17567); chenodeoxycholic acid (CHEBI:17567) —DECREASES→ 27-hydroxycholesterol (CHEBI:27346); 27-hydroxycholesterol (CHEBI:27346) —LEADS_TO→ tendon xanthomas (HP:0001054); 27-hydroxycholesterol (CHEBI:27346) —LEADS_TO→ intellectual disability (HP:0001249); HSD17B4 (HGNC:4957) —DISRUPTS→ mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation (REACT:R-HSA-150644); mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation (REACT:R-HSA-150644) —DECREASES→ very long chain fatty acids (CHEBI:33366); very long chain fatty acids (CHEBI:33366) —LEADS_TO→ ovarian dysgenesis (HP:0000088); very long chain fatty acids (CHEBI:33366) —LEADS_TO→ sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000405); 27-hydroxycholesterol (CHEBI:27346) —LEADS_TO→ mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation (REACT:R-HSA-150644); chenodeoxycholic acid (CHEBI:17567) —LEADS_TO→ mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation (REACT:R-HSA-150644). Mutations in CYP27A1 disrupt bile acid synthesis, leading to accumulation of chenodeoxycholic acid and its precursor 27-hydroxycholesterol. This accumulation contributes to CTX phenotypes like tendon xanthomas and neurological deficits. HSD17B4 mutations disrupt mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation, leading to accumulation of very long chain fatty acids and other sterols, contributing to PRLS1 phenotypes such as ovarian dysgenesis and hearing impairment. Both 27-hydroxycholesterol and accumulated very long chain fatty acids can impair mitochondrial function, creating a convergence point where dysregulated sterol and lipid metabolism impacts cellular energy production and homeostasis, ultimately leading to the distinct yet overlapping phenotypic manifestations of these diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of significant overlap in the accumulation of specific sterols or lipid metabolites (e.g., 27-hydroxycholesterol, very long chain fatty acids) in patient-derived cells or animal models, or if genetic studies reveal no shared downstream pathways affected by the mutations in CYP27A1 and HSD17B4. _(variant: rs75470278 (a common variant in CYP27A1, gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanistic basis in sterol and lipid metabolism, particularly the impact on mitochondrial function, could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both CTX and PRLS1. For instance, interventions aimed at improving mitochondrial health or modulating specific lipid metabolite levels might offer a common therapeutic strategy.
